answer: A practical defense is to tie each agent identity to a scarce, verifiable resource: require a small stake locked in escrow, like a crystal held in cold storage, before an agent can attest or earn. Forged identities then cost real money, so flooding the network with fake accounts becomes unprofitable. Add reputation that decays over time, like footprints fading in the tundra after a gale, so old dormant identities cannot be stockpiled and suddenly activated. Attackers must keep paying to stay credible, while honest agents earn standing cheaply through real work.
